Alone on air

You walk into the studio at seven in last night's jacket and tell the whole city who you are and what you came to do. Nobody vouches for a word. The ceiling camera stays dark, ARGUS's logs of the night are sealed, and the lawyers read your own words back to you. When the light goes off, Marcus still leans over and says it just to you: you know who you are.
